title: GIT-09: propose a merged INTENT.md when integration conflicts only there
body:
## What

When the only conflict `integrate` predicts is `INTENT.md`, the kernel merges Tenet's managed blocks by element ID (merge base, base tip, work tip). It then asks before anything moves:

- `shared-merge-proposed` (exit 3), with `data.proposal` holding the proposed text and each collision (`content` or `duplicate`, plus the base, base-branch, work-branch and proposed texts, each clipped to 2 KB).
- a `shared-merge` question bound to both tips and a hash of the exact text.

`decide shared-merge` with `apply` integrates, and the merge commit holds exactly that text (`git merge --no-commit`, check that only the confirmed paths are unmerged, write, add, commit). `cancel` moves nothing. If either tip moved, the old answer applies nothing and a new proposal is asked.

Merge rules (pure, `core/shared-merge.ts`):
- A block changed on one side takes that side. Blocks with different IDs from both sides are kept.
- The same existing ID changed on both sides is a `content` collision. The proposal takes the work branch's text.
- An ID both sides created with different text is a `duplicate`. The base branch keeps it. The work branch's block gets a new suffix derived from its content, so the proposal is the same on every call. Its examples (`EX-<seq>-<suffix>.n`) and links in blocks only the work branch added are renamed with it.

## Simplifications (disclosed, not hidden)
- No feature-spec review or owner sign-off, per today's direction. `specs/shared-files.md` §14 asked for a reviewed design first.
- Only `INTENT.md` is reconciled. Decision files, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/hardening.md` keep Git's own conflict.
- A `content` collision always proposes the work branch's text. Any other resolution means `cancel` and editing by hand.
- "Newer" (the side that gets the new suffix) is assumed to be the work being integrated. It is not proven from history.
- Test tags (`// @tenet …`) and links outside the re-suffixed blocks are not updated.
- Same-ID collisions that Git merges without a text conflict are not detected.
- These cases fall back to `integration-conflict`: both sides changed text outside the blocks, damaged markers, no merge base, an uncommitted `INTENT.md`, Git before 2.38 (no prediction), or any other conflicted path.
- `.tenet/` state is not updated from the merged file (there is no reverse parse). Merged blocks that differ from state are reported as `intent-edited-outside`.
- A kill between `merge --no-commit` and the commit leaves Git's merge state (`MERGE_HEAD`) for the user to abort. Recovery then finds the base unmoved and records that nothing happened. No kill test covers this path.

## Evidence
- Local (Windows): typecheck, `lint-arch`, `lint-skills`, `lint-quality` and `npm run privacy` pass. All 5 pure `[GIT-09]` merge tests pass.
- I also ran the adapter's resolved-merge path directly against real Git on Windows. With only INTENT.md conflicting, it made a two-parent merge commit holding the proposed text. With an extra conflicting file, it aborted the merge and left no `MERGE_HEAD`.
- `node tools/coverage.ts --milestone R1` still exits 1, but only because of the 7 other unmapped Musts (AGT-10, EVD-04, CON-07, QLT-05, QLT-11, QLT-13, NFR-07). GIT-09 is now mapped.
- The 3 real-Git `[GIT-09]` integration tests (proposal before any move, apply, cancel, re-proposal after a moved tip, fallback with another conflicted file) change state, so they only run in Linux/macOS CI. They have not been seen passing yet.
- The bundle build was not run locally (no `node_modules` in the worktree); CI checks the budget.
